Symmetric Proportionality

Source: R/proportionality.r
phi_s.Rd

The symmetric proportionality measure \(\phi_s\) of Quinn et al. (2017), propr's "phs": the variance of the log ratio of two features relative to that of their log product. 0 means perfectly proportional.

Usage

phi_s(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  denominator = NULL,
  pseudocount = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of non-negative abundances (samples \(\times\) features), or any of the objects listed under Input Types. Counts, proportions, and the output of replace_zeros() are all accepted: each sample's scale cancels out of the log ratios. Pairs are taken between the features (the columns when margin = 1), and the variance is over the samples.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

denominator

The reference that each feature's log abundance is taken relative to, for the variances \(\mathrm{var}(z_i)\). NULL (the default) uses the centered log ratio (clr): each sample's geometric mean of all features, as propr's default ivar = "clr". Otherwise features, as names, (1-based) indices, or a logical vector with one value per feature: their geometric mean. One feature gives the additive log ratio (alr, as alr(denominator =)), and that feature is then left out of the result (its alr is 0 in every sample); with several, every feature is kept.

pseudocount

Added to every value before taking logs. NULL (the default) adds nothing when counts has no zeros, and otherwise uses half the smallest non-zero value, with a warning. 0 adds nothing, and is an error when counts has zeros. See Zeros.

clust

Whether and how to cluster the samples (rows and columns) before returning the distance matrix: NULL (the default) or FALSE to keep them in their input order, or one of stats::hclust()'s linkage methods, "average" (UPGMA), "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty" (WPGMA), "median" or "centroid", or "pcoa" to order them along the first axis of pcoa(). Clustering reorders the samples of the result, with their labels (samples without names are labelled with their positions in the input): its order attribute gives each one's position in the input, so that meta[attr(d, "order"), ] lines metadata up with them. ecodive's ordinations and tests put the samples back in their input order before analysing them, so give them metadata in its usual order. Other packages see the reordered matrix: give them metadata reordered by order, or matched by name. The matrix's display list keeps clust (FALSE as "none"; see ecodive_display), which plot.ecodive_dist() follows: with NULL it clusters the samples for the heatmap ("average"), and with "none" it keeps their order. clust needs every distance, so it cannot be used with pairs. rho_p()'s similarities are clustered as \(1 - \rho_p\).

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), will use all logical CPU cores.

Value

A dist object over the features, as rho_p() returns, with method "phi_s". It is a dissimilarity, so it can be given as dm to pcoa(), dist_ord() or stats::hclust().

Details

With \(z\) the log-ratio-transformed abundances (clr or alr), $$\phi_{s,ij} = \frac{\mathrm{var}(z_i - z_j)}{\mathrm{var}(z_i + z_j)} = \frac{1 - \rho_{p,ij}}{1 + \rho_{p,ij}}$$ where \(\mathrm{var}(z_i - z_j)\) is vlr() and \(\rho_p\) is rho_p(). It lies in \([0, \infty)\): 0 for proportional features, 1 for unrelated ones, and infinite for reciprocal ones (\(z_i = -z_j\)). It is computed as \(\mathrm{vlr}_{ij} / (2\mathrm{var}(z_i) + 2\mathrm{var}(z_j) - \mathrm{vlr}_{ij})\), since \(\mathrm{var}(a + b) = 2\mathrm{var}(a) + 2\mathrm{var}(b) - \mathrm{var}(a - b)\). Unlike vlr(), it depends on the denominator. Near-reciprocal pairs (such as the two features of a two-feature denominator, whose \(z\) are exact opposites) have \(\mathrm{var}(z_i + z_j)\) near 0, where rounding dominates: their value is Inf or merely very large.

Lovell et al.'s (2015) original \(\phi = \mathrm{vlr}_{ij} / \mathrm{var}(z_i)\) is not symmetric (\(\phi_{ij} \ne \phi_{ji}\)), so it can't be a dist; Quinn et al. (2017) replaced it with \(\phi_s\). This is the measure that propr computes with propr(counts, metric = "phs") (see Zeros for its zero handling).

Zeros

Logs of zero are undefined, so zeros need replacing first. With pseudocount = NULL (the default), no pseudocount is used when counts has no zeros; otherwise half the smallest non-zero value is added to every value, with a warning. The recommended input is a table with its zeros replaced by replace_zeros(), which has none and is used as it is.

propr (Quinn et al. 2017) replaces only the zeros, by 1, which is not pseudocount = 1 (that adds 1 to every value). To reproduce it, write x[x == 0] <- 1 and then call these functions on x.

Pseudocounts are not neutral: in sparse tables the many zeros, all given the same value, can dominate the variances. Filtering out rare features first helps.

Size

The result has \(D(D - 1)/2\) values: 20,000 features give 2e8 pairs, 1.6 GB. Filter out rare features first for large tables. The table itself stays sparse.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Lovell, D., Pawlowsky-Glahn, V., Egozcue, J. J., Marguerat, S., & Bähler, J. (2015). Proportionality: a valid alternative to correlation for relative data. PLoS Computational Biology, 11, e1004075.

Quinn, T. P., Richardson, M. F., Lovell, D., & Crowley, T. M. (2017). propr: an R-package for identifying proportionally abundant features using compositional data analysis. Scientific Reports, 7, 16252.

See also

vlr(), rho_p(), replace_zeros().

Examples

    x <- replace_zeros(ex_counts, 'mult')
    phi_s(x)
#> # A dist: 6 features (lower triangle)
#> # Proportionality (phi_s)
#>                   Streptococcus Bacteroides Corynebacterium Haemophilus
#> Bacteroides              3.03
#> Corynebacterium          0.843         4.65
#> Haemophilus              0.0725        1.55           1.94
#> Propionibacterium       29.7           0.53           0.662      119
#> Staphylococcus           2.62          2.4            0.211        3.31
#> # … 1 more column: Propionibacterium
#> # Attributes: method

    # The same as (1 - rho_p) / (1 + rho_p)
    rho <- rho_p(x)
    all.equal(c(phi_s(x)), c((1 - rho) / (1 + rho)))
#> [1] TRUE
